question: Which of the following best describes the theme of the book Why Bharat Matters?

options.text: Ancient mythology of India and festival
Fictional rural story and moral values

solution:
The correct answer is __**India's economic and cultural importance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Why Bharat Matters** emphasizes the pivotal role of India in global economic, cultural, and political spheres.
 
• The book highlights India's **economic growth trajectory**, focusing on its rising significance in international trade and commerce.
 
• It explores India's **cultural heritage and diversity**, showcasing how its traditions, languages, and philosophies have influenced the world.
 
• The narrative delves into India’s **strategic geopolitical position**, illustrating its importance in global diplomacy and regional stability.
 
• The book also underscores India’s contributions to technology, education, and sustainable development, reinforcing its status as a global powerhouse.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Influential Indian Authors & Works**

 
 
• Rabindranath Tagore: Gitanjali, The Post Office (poetry, spirituality).
 
• Mahatma Gandhi: The Story of My Experiments with Truth (autobiography).
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru: The Discovery of India, Glimpses of World History (history, Indian context).
 
• R.K. Narayan: Malgudi Days, The Guide (slice-of-life fiction).
 
• Mulk Raj Anand: Untouchable, The Private Life of an Indian Prince (social realism).
 
• Arundhati Roy: The God of Small Things (family, society).
 
• Aravind Adiga: The White Tiger (class, corruption).
 
• Jhumpa Lahiri: Interpreter of Maladies, Whereabouts (identity, displacement).
